Residents shouldn't have to guess which agency to call or repeat their story at every counter. With Unison, a person makes one request and gets one reference. An orchestrator brings in every agency needed, with consent, while each agency keeps its own systems and data.

• Enterprise: the same pattern works as one front door across HR, IT, facilities and finance, so employees and customers ask once and every team behind it acts.

Grateful to win Gold for Grab in the Employer Branding category at the HR Excellence Awards Indonesia 2026, recognizing the region’s most impactful HR initiatives.

Indonesia’s talent market shifted this year due to recent macroeconomic situation. Tighter tech funding slowed hiring, and many professionals has limited access to world-class AI tools and learning curve they need to build skills and keep pace globally.

At Grab, we don’t build AI capability by simply hiring more AI talent. We grow the ecosystem that creates it. So we went beyond storytelling and EVP selling, and stopped waiting for great talent to come to us. We grew with the communities they already belong to.

Partnering with OpenAI, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud, we put Grab’s tech experts and leaders on stage to mentor and open our AI learning to Indonesia’s tech community. 𝗠𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳𝗳𝘀𝗵𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝗵𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘁𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗮 𝗷𝗼𝗯 𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗹𝗲.

"We need a developer." "We need an accountant." "We need a customer support agent." It sounds like a clear brief, but a job title says very little about the work itself. Two companies hiring a "marketing executive" may need completely different skills, hours, and experience levels.

That's why we suggest starting one step earlier, with the work:
1. 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 that needs to get done every week.
2. 𝗦𝗼𝗿𝘁 𝗶𝘁. What needs your core team, what can a dedicated team in Southeast Asia own, and what can tools or AI support?
3. 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽 𝗿𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲𝘀. Together, they show the team you actually need.
4. 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝗰𝗵 𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁. Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines each have different strengths, so the best country for one role may not be the best for another.

When the work is clear, the hiring decisions that follow (role, location, budget, and employment setup) get much easier. 𝘚𝘵𝘢𝘳𝘵 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘬. 𝘉𝘶𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘩𝘵 𝘚𝘰𝘶𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘵 𝘈𝘴𝘪𝘢 𝘵𝘦𝘢𝘮.

posts.text:
The mistake I see most from companies hiring in Indonesia is paying a full-time engineer as a "contractor" through Wise or PayPal.

It feels clean: no entity, no payroll, one transfer a month.

But Indonesian law looks at how the work actually happens, not at what the contract calls it. Regular hours, consistent work and a long-term engagement make it employment. Once it's employment:
- BPJS social security applies, and authorities can make you pay the missed contributions back, with penalties.
- THR, a full extra month's wage every year, is owed.
- Ending it goes through Indonesia's termination process and severance rules. There's no at-will employment.

It also hurts retention. Strong Indonesian developers increasingly expect full legal employment with BPJS, and a contractor setup for what is really a full-time job is the kind they leave.

Fixing it doesn't need an Indonesian entity. An Employer of Record becomes the legal employer and handles the contract, BPJS, tax and THR, while you keep running the work day to day.

Using the ABCD method: Strategies in misinformation prevention among older adults (Jurnal Studi Komunikasi):

https://lnkd.in/dwnTZuB6

Glimpse: Using the ABCD framework (Observe, Read, Verify, and Discuss) as an analytical lens, this qualitative study investigates how older persons evaluate and react to unverified material in digital environments. Ten participants, ages 61 to 72, were interviewed in Surabaya, Indonesia. The results indicate that participants routinely check message senders, read text in its entirety, ask for explanation online or from others, and debate dubious information—most often with family members. Verification procedures, however, are inconsistent and frequently prioritize sender identity over original sources. The study emphasizes how social networks affect information evaluation and proposes that reading, verifying, and watching are separate but related digital literacy abilities. Overall, the results show a variety of spontaneous checking and correcting activities, challenging presumptions that older persons communicate false information and mindlessly trust it.
